name: Leeks
why_now: Leeks come into their own as the weather cools. Cooked slowly, they melt into something soft and sweet that turns a braise or a soup into a cool-weather dish.
how_to_choose: Straight, firm white and light-green parts
Medium leeks are more tender than very thick ones
buy_this_much: 4 for the suggested week: two for the braise, two for the minestrone.
price_note: Sold singly or in bunches of two or three.

flavor_paths.name: Melted
flavor_paths.description: Butter, salt, ten minutes on low with the lid on.

flavor_paths.name: Braised
flavor_paths.description: Under chicken thighs, with fennel and satsuma.

flavor_paths.name: In soup
flavor_paths.description: The first thing in the pot.

weekday_uses: Softened in sausage fat to start the minestrone
Left over from the braise, on toast with an egg
weekend_use: Softened with fennel under the braised chicken thighs.
storage: In the fridge, unwashed, for up to two weeks.
one_thing_to_learn: Leeks hold grit between their layers. Slice them first, then swish the slices in a bowl of cold water and lift them out with your hands; the sand sinks to the bottom.
